note_tweet.text:
SpaceX $SPCX said a lot more on the call than in the release:

1. Q1 2027 revenue guided to $33B to $37B. The Street was near $22.2B. That is more than double Q3.

2. Q4 capex guided to $35B to $40B, nearly double Q3.

3. Backlog of $63B, with about $42B expected to be recognized within a year.

4. Compute is renting slightly above the top of the $30 to $50 per watt range given last quarter. Payback is under a year, and contracts are renewing at higher prices.

5. $SPCX keeps compute on short-term contracts at spot rates and splits it roughly 50/50 between its own use and renting out.

6. Grok Bot reached 800,000 paid weekly users, more than doubling in a month.

7. A 440,000 Vera Rubin training cluster is targeted by the end of Q2 2027.

8. SpaceX casts its own turbine blades and vanes. Musk says that brings power online 12 to 18 months faster than rivals.

9. Starship weekly in H1 2027, twice weekly by H2. The Flight 15 license is expected to include tower catches of both stages.

10. Starlink targets about 100x today's bandwidth within roughly three years, on around 100,000 satellites. Musk sees a path to several hundred billion dollars a year in connectivity revenue.

11. Roughly 12,000 aircraft are contracted for Starlink, almost a quarter of the world's fleet.

12. Starlink Mobile has 22M monthly users, +37% QoQ. The FCC approved 15,000 Mobile V2 satellites, and US service is targeted for early 2028.

13. Terafab is aiming for a first test chip around May or June 2027 and volume production around Q3 2028.

14. Both SpaceX and Tesla $TSLA have special committees on a merger. No agreement on terms, and Tesla would need a majority of all shares.

Elon Musk $SPCX, Chief Executive Officer:
'𝙎𝙤 𝙬𝙚 𝙘𝙤𝙪𝙡𝙙 𝙧𝙚𝙣𝙩 𝙤𝙪𝙩 𝙤𝙪𝙧 𝙘𝙤𝙢𝙥𝙪𝙩𝙚 𝙨𝙚𝙫𝙚𝙧𝙖𝙡 𝙩𝙞𝙢𝙚𝙨 𝙤𝙫𝙚𝙧 𝙞𝙛 𝙬𝙚 𝙨𝙖𝙞𝙙 𝙮𝙚𝙨 𝙩𝙤 𝙚𝙫𝙚𝙧𝙮𝙤𝙣𝙚.'

Q4 gross margin is expected to slip back toward Q2 levels after one-time Q3 benefits, including about 3 points of tariff refunds in Connectivity.

Tuesday 20 October 2026 SpaceX TA

SpaceX just guided Q1 2027 to $33B-$37B. One quarter, more than all of 2026 so far ($27.1B). This is the beat nobody modeled, and after hours already ripped to $158.19, straight through the top of the box and the gap. Tomorrow's close above $151 is the formality.

Today $SPCX closed at $147.79, down 0.11% from Monday's $147.96. On Monday I said $145-$146 should hold through Q3. It didn't: the open flushed it to $143.27. I said if it lost $145-$146, $140-$143 was next. Missed by 27 cents, and the first hour closed back at $147.90. I said holding would put $154 back in play. Not in the regular session, but after hours printed $158.25. I said a daily close under $140 would make my bull case wrong. Never even close.

Then 4pm happened. Revenue $14.58B vs $12.7B-$13B expected. AI did $7.56B, almost 3x last quarter and more than rockets and Starlink combined. $4.40B of profit, after a $541M loss last quarter.

And the call was even bigger. Q1 2027 guided 35-51% above the ~$24.5B the Street had. Elon said SpaceX could exit 2027 at $500B to $1T of annual recurring revenue, against a company worth about $2.1T after hours. He'd be surprised by less than 13 GW of compute by the end of next year. They have 1.7 GW today. Grok Bot hit 800,000 paid weekly users, more than double in a month. Flight 15 tries to catch the ship. Starlink is on 12,000 aircraft. First Terafab test chip May/June 2027.

The stock closed at $147.79 like none of this was coming. It's coming.

The chart was ready for it. $143.27 held above Friday's $142.95, and the day printed a hammer at the bottom of a $140.66-$151.01 box on 89.4M shares, 9% above the 20-day average. Sellers flushed the open and got absorbed: closed $4.52 off the low. Nobody dumped into the print.

The box is $10.35 tall, so a daily close above $151.01 measures to $161, right where the 8-12 Oct lows sat. After hours already went through the 21-day average at about $153 and the $155.44-$156.05 gap. From the close, upside to $176.42 is about 3.7 times the downside to $140.

Wednesday's map: daily close above $151 and I expect $161 fast, then $176.42. A gap up that closes back under $151 would be a failed breakout, and that's the only thing that changes my mind short term. Daily close under $143 and I expect a retest of $140.66.

My view: this morning I said a huge beat means $176 by Friday. We got $14.58B, $7.56B from AI, and a Q1 guide bigger than the first nine months of this year. I'm not just sticking with it, I'm pressing it. Up to 1.3B shares unlock Thursday and I don't care. Numbers like this eat unlocks. $161 is the first stop. $176.42 is next.

Key levels:
First support: $143-$145
Strong support: $140-$141
Bulls in control above: $151 (daily close)
Targets: $161, $176.42
Bull case wrong below: daily close < $140
